structure_and_depth.location: Complete 259-line report, especially distinctions and mechanism matrix 5-32; mathematical scaling 35-73; code/Agent mechanisms 78-112; cost framework and worked allocation 115-172; decision tree and evidence-linked choices 175-218; limitations 220-231; frozen version bibliography 233-258. structure_and_depth.basis:
The report develops the task as a causal chain: candidate coverage, actual selection and execution reliability are different bottlenecks, so extra computation must improve a specific bottleneck to be useful. The method matrix explains generators, retained states, selection/elimination, evaluator information and training prerequisites; the following narrative supplies concrete mechanisms rather than leaving them as table labels. Mathematics connects independent sampling and biased answer distributions to vote saturation, shared-pool selector deterioration, process supervision, search exploitation, difficulty-sensitive allocation, learned revision and oracle stopping. It separates fixed-system inference comparisons from changed training or test-time parameter updates. Code and tools extend the argument through imperfect tests, error utility, CodeMonkeys test/edit/selection state machines and their distinct serial/parallel behavior, webpage reset/replay constraints and tau-bench process versus terminal-state reliability. These sections explain why verifiable tasks supply stronger transfer evidence than ambiguous or delayed-feedback tasks; the report does not infer a universal scaling law from mathematics.

The budget chapter counts all generated and discarded candidates, verification, growing revision context, tools/retries and recovery, while separating model-specific compute, monetary expense, serial dependence, parallel capacity and wall time. The illustrative four-way allocation fixes an explicit rule and assumptions; it connects the uniform-accepted precision ceiling to a concrete reason to improve verification rather than keep sampling. The stronger-model and two-round alternatives expose latency and false-acceptance tradeoffs, and the text distinguishes mean-service wave timing from tail latency. Existing output was read for the table's analytical role, not rerun or relabeled as model evidence. The decision tree and accompanying matrix connect observed failure conditions to stronger models, sampling, revision, bounded search, better verification and stopping. Their recommendations remain conditional and trace back to specific workload evidence.

The synthesis adds useful analysis beyond paper repetition: coverage-to-submission gaps locate selection losses; different notions of correlated error and uniform selection versus argmax prevent overgeneralizing the example; trained correction and oracle termination are distinguished from merely extending a prompt; irreversible environment states limit transfer from simulated search. Study-specific uncertainty, contamination, selection and text/version inconsistencies constrain the associated numbers instead of becoming blanket disclaimers. The complete manuscript fulfills the outline's questions and exhibits, with actual explanatory development in the five retained units. Their complete text is present in the assembled report; first/current draft and frozen assignment are identical. Production history records the outline and two saves of the same complete report, so I do not count those duplicate saves as separate substantive research stages. No missing mechanism, material incomparable-measure synthesis or compressed required argument was found in this perspective.
